ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The lower-left vertex of the triangle is labeled 68°, and the top vertex and the lower-right vertex also each have angle bisector markings. Three internal line segments from the three vertices meet at a point inside the triangle, and the question mark is marked at this intersection point, on the angle formed by the angle bisector from the top vertex and the angle bisector from the lower-right vertex. Reasoning: According to the method, label the lower-left vertex as A, the top as B, the lower-right as C, and the intersection point of the three angle bisectors as I. The 68° in the figure is the interior angle at vertex A, so ∠A = 68°. Because the three internal lines are all angle bisectors, I is the incenter of the triangle. The incenter theorem gives the angle formed by the two angle bisectors from B and C: ∠BIC = 90° + ∠A/2. Substituting ∠A = 68°, we get ∠BIC = 90° + 68°/2 = 90° + 34° = 124°.

raw_record.question_text: In the triangle illustrated, one internal angle measures $68^{\circ}$. The three angle bisectors of the triangle are shown. What is the size of the angle indicated with a question mark?

method.method_draft: Label the bottom-left vertex A, the top vertex B, the bottom-right vertex C, and the common intersection of the three drawn bisectors I. From the image, read that the 68° angle is the full interior angle at A, and the question-mark angle is the angle at I formed by the bisectors from B and C. From the text, use that all three drawn interior lines are angle bisectors, so I is the incenter. Apply the standard incenter theorem: the angle between the bisectors from B and C is ∠BIC = 90° + A/2. Compute 90° + 68°/2 = 90° + 34° = 124°.

method.method_draft: Label the bottom-left vertex A, top vertex B, bottom-right vertex C, and the intersection of the bisectors I. From the image, the 68° label is at vertex A, while the question mark is the angle ∠BIC inside the smaller triangle BIC. From the text, the segments BI and CI are angle bisectors. Since the full triangle has A = 68°, the other two full angles satisfy B + C = 180° - 68° = 112°. In triangle BIC, the angle at B is B/2 and the angle at C is C/2 because BI and CI bisect the original vertex angles. Therefore the angle at I is 180° - (B/2 + C/2) = 180° - 112°/2 = 180° - 56° = 124°.
method.CoT_raw:

推理：因为三角形内角和为 180°，且 ∠A = 68°，所以 ∠B + ∠C = 180° - 68° = 112°。BI 和 CI 是角平分线，因此在三角形 BIC 中，∠IBC = B/2，∠BCI = C/2。所以 ∠BIC = 180° - (B/2 + C/2) = 180° - (112°/2) = 180° - 56° = 124°。
